THOUGHT: The patient is a woman in her 30s with progressive bilateral nasal obstruction from a voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascular sinonasal mass. Imaging shows a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity plus a thyroid lesion and bone metastases (5th rib, L4). MRI confirms anterior skull base extension. Radioiodine scintigraphy shows uptake in the rib and vertebral lesions but low uptake in the sinonasal tumor (compatible with thyroid tissue of low iodine avidity). Serum thyroglobulin is markedly elevated (4432 ng/mL), and biopsy of both rib and sinonasal lesions confirmed thyroid carcinoma metastasis. Taken together, the data strongly indicate a metastatic thyroid carcinoma presenting with an unusual hypervascular sinonasal metastasis. Follicular-type thyroid carcinomas (including oncocytic/Hürthle-cell variants) characteristically metastasize hematogenously to bone, frequently raise thyroglobulin, and some variants (Hürthle cell or poorly differentiated components) have low radioiodine avidity and can be relatively hypervascular — matching this presentation. Other considerations (renal cell carcinoma metastasis to the nose, primary hypervascular sinonasal tumors like angiofibroma or hemangiopericytoma, or metastatic other primaries) are less likely given the concordant thyroid lesion, the very high thyroglobulin, and biopsy confirmation of thyroid origin.

DIAGNOSIS:
1. Metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma (including Hürthle-cell/oncocytic variant) with sinonasal and bone metastases
2. Metastatic poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma (insular/poorly differentiated component) with low RAI avidity
3. Metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma with distant spread (less likely given bone-predominant spread and low sinonasal RAI uptake)
4. Metastasis to the nasal cavity from a hypervascular non-thyroid primary (e.g., renal cell carcinoma) — differential consideration for a hypervascular/pulsatile nasal mass
5. Primary hypervascular sinonasal neoplasm (e.g., hemangiopericytoma/solitary fibrous tumor, sinonasal paraganglioma, juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma) — less likely given thyroid lesion, Tg elevation, and biopsy confirmation of thyroid origin
ground_truth: Radioiodine-refractory vesicular thyroid carcinoma (VTC) with sinonasal metastasis
